scbench.reference: SCBench, Section 3.1 and Table 2 (task categories and membership); Table 3 (task components)
notes: The official benchmark contains 12 base tasks; our prepared evaluated suite contains 11, omitting Chinese question answering (Zh.QA) from semantic retrieval.
Group task keys refer to base tasks. Prepared mid, short, and tiny variants inherit their base task's category and must be identified separately from the 11-base-task summaries.

The official paper separates Many-shot ICL into date understanding, salient translation-error detection, and tracking seven shuffled objects, and describes the two components of each mixed task. These components are not stored as separate scores in the method-scores snapshot; retain the evaluated combined tasks rather than infer component scores.
Multi-turn and multi-request are shared-context evaluation modes, not task categories. The paper's compressible/incompressible discussion does not provide an exhaustive task partition.

ruler.reference: RULER, Sections 3.1–3.4 (categories), Section 3.1 (retrieval subtypes), Appendix B/Table 5 (13 concrete configurations), Appendix F/Table 13 (eight-task retrieval mean)
notes: Group task keys omit the ruler_ prefix and context-length suffix. Apply categories separately at each evaluated context length.

All 13 configurations are evaluated at 4K and 8K. At 64K only seven are evaluated: niah_single_1, niah_multikey_3, niah_multivalue, vt, cwe, fwe, and qa_2. Label the 64K benchmark mean as a selected seven-task mean.

At 64K, retrieval covers 3 of 8 official configurations, multi-hop tracing covers 1 of 1, aggregation covers 2 of 2, and question answering covers 1 of 2. Single NIAH and Multi-keys NIAH each cover 1 of 3; Multi-values NIAH covers 1 of 1; Multi-queries NIAH has no evaluated configuration.
Single-configuration categories or retrieval subtypes coincide with the corresponding individual task plot; identify this relationship explicitly rather than treating them as new measurements.
